solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bachelor born in Leon ripped hamstring

indicators.note: something ripped is torn apart, so the letters of the Spanish city name are pulled out of order
placed in says the two single letters sit inside the rearranged city name

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor
b. is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
the city name taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A footballer, a bachelor born in the Spanish city of Leon, has torn his hamstring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamstring' sits at the end like part of the injury story, but it is the verb being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble is to disable or cripple a person or horse, just as hamstringing someone lames them.

clue.text: Extinct language from ex-wife in Bow?

blocks.note: an ex is a former or old partner
in Cockney speech, as heard in Bow in east London, a man's wife is his dutch

explanation.surface: A dead tongue apparently learnt from a former wife in an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an East End district of London, home of Cockneys, who call a wife 'my old dutch' (from duchess). Here 'ex' is only OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Dutch is the early medieval form of the Dutch language, spoken centuries ago and long since dead.

clue.text: Imagine having squandered 500 sheets!

indicators.note: having squandered means having wasted and so lost the roman numeral for that number

blocks.note: to imagine something is to dream it
D is the roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An exclamation of amazement at someone wasting five hundred sheets of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: DREAM loses its D (500) to leave REAM; the 500 does double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is the traditional stationery quantity of paper, nowadays standardised at five hundred sheets.

clue.text: Bump from slow boat damaged creel

indicators.note: a damaged fishing basket is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a tub is a clumsy, slow-moving boat
the fishing basket taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An angler's fishing basket was dented when knocked by a slow old boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tubercle is a small rounded swelling or nodule, on a bone, plant or skin, so a little bump.

clue.text: Was forced to bury headless tyrant in bunker?

indicators.note: headless says the Russian ruler's title loses its first letter
to bury something is to put it inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: had (to), as in 'he had to go', means was forced
a tzar was an absolute Russian ruler, a tyrant

explanation.surface: A dictator was forced to inter a decapitated tyrant in an underground shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunker' looks like a wartime shelter; the question mark points to golf.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course a bunker is a sand trap, which the game classes as a hazard alongside water.

clue.text: Italian novelist keeping hard copy

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the novelist's name surrounds the letter

blocks.note: Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An Italian writer holds on to a hard copy of his manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a repetition or imitation of something, so it serves as a copy of the original.

clue.text: Money difficulties checked at the outset

indicators.note: checked means stopped, and at the outset means right at the start, so the first letter is halted and dropped

blocks.note: trouble means problems or difficulties

explanation.surface: Financial problems that were brought under control early on.
explanation.walkthrough: TROUBLE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency unit of Russia, so a form of money.

clue.text: Kinky one said to smooth down rubber

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of the number word are twisted round
said means spoken, so the word for smoothing feathers is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the number word taken letter for letter
to preen is to smooth down feathers or hair

explanation.surface: A kinky person is said to smooth down a rubber outfit, a fetish joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoprene is a synthetic rubber used for wetsuits and similar garments.

clue.text: Star here exhausted – winger unable to move

indicators.note: the letters are made to move into a new order

blocks.note: an owl is a bird, a winged creature
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An exhausted winger stuck on the pitch, unable to move, sees stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer, but it is a bird. The definition is cryptic: a planetary nebula is the shell of gas left by a burnt-out star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Owl Nebula is a planetary nebula in Ursa Major, gas thrown off by a dying star whose fuel ran out.

clue.text: Call cricketing pair effective at both ends after century

indicators.note: at both ends asks for only the first and last letters of the word
after says the remaining pieces follow the abbreviation for a hundred

blocks.note: C is the roman numeral for a hundred, and a century is a hundred
in cricket a pair is two ducks, scoring nought in both innings
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator's verdict on a pair of batsmen who each scored effectively at both ends after a century.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket century is a hundred runs; a pair is out for nought (O) twice, giving OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooee is a shrill call used to attract attention at a distance, originally an Australian bush cry.

clue.text: Act stupid to make things unclear

blocks.note: to act a part is to be someone
dim means slow-witted

explanation.surface: Playing the fool deliberately to muddy the waters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedim is to make dim, obscuring sight or understanding.

clue.text: Inspiration from singer at opera

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of singer, all of at and the start of opera

explanation.surface: A soprano's performance at the opera house is inspiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry, and a muse is a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Planes flying our flag start to pitch and roll

indicators.note: start to asks for just the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: British Airways, the British flag-carrier airline
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Airliners with the national flag on the tail begin to pitch and roll in turbulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch and roll' reads as aircraft motion, but roll is the definition. A flag carrier is a country's national airline.
explanation.definitionFit: A bap is a soft, flattish bread roll, as used for a bacon sandwich in Britain.

clue.text: Controversial seminars course is in Latin

blocks.note: first meaning: Erhard Seminars Training, a controversial 1970s self-help course
second meaning: the Latin for 'is'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a disputed seminar taught in Latin; the two halves are separate meanings of the same three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Erhard Seminars Training was a much-criticised personal-development programme, and the Latin verb 'to be' has third person 'est' for 'is'.

clue.text: Anglicans’ leader, his credo CE, revived appropriate district

indicators.note: leader means the letter at the head of the word
revived means brought back to life in a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken letter for letter; CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The Anglican leader revives his Church of England creed in a suitable area.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'appropriate district', apt because the surface is about the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdiocese is the area under an archbishop's jurisdiction, a church district fitting for the Anglican scene.

clue.text: States not entirely hostile

indicators.note: not entirely means not quite whole, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: averse means opposed or hostile

explanation.surface: Countries that are not wholly unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a noun for countries; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, so avers means asserts or states.

clue.text: Author in love with son starts show

indicators.note: in says the word for writing sits inside the letter shaped like zero
with says the abbreviation is added on alongside

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to author is to write or pen
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A writer in love with his son begins a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a show is to start it, so 'opens' and 'starts show' both describe getting a performance underway.

clue.text: Say jumper‘s left among articles by hollow tree

indicators.note: among means placed in the midst of the articles
hollow means emptied of its middle, so only the outer letters are left
by means next to, so the last piece follows on

blocks.note: A and THE, the indefinite and definite articles
L is the abbreviation for left
only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A sweater has been left among some items next to a hollow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside THE, after A, then TE. 'Jumper' suggests a sweater; 'Say' marks it as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A high or long jumper is one kind of athlete, so 'Say jumper' points to the broader class by example.

clue.text: I’ve collapsed in pain society creates

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen in a heap, so the contraction's letters are jumbled
in says the jumbled letters sit inside the word for pain

blocks.note: an ache is a pain
the contraction taken letter for letter
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed in agony at what society produces.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to bring it about, so achieves loosely means brings into being or creates.

clue.text: Burn up old woman in Greek island

indicators.note: in places the word for an elderly woman inside the island's name

blocks.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman gets sunburnt on a Greek island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate is to reduce a dead body to ashes by burning.

clue.text: Lament for dead king taking place in Hackney?

indicators.note: in says the pieces before it go inside the word for a hired carriage

blocks.note: R is short for rex, king
an event that is on is happening, taking place
a hackney is a horse-drawn coach for hire

explanation.surface: A dirge for a dead monarch held in a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hackney' looks like the London borough; the question mark flags it as a hackney carriage, a coach. 'Dead king' tempts as one unit, but king belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronach is a Scottish or Irish funeral dirge, a song of mourning for the dead.

clue.text: Missile‘s first-rate: with roar it exploded

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a kind of missile

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters fly into a new order

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A top-class missile exploding with a roar.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 becomes AI because the digit 1 looks like the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-to-air describes a missile fired from one aircraft at another in flight.

clue.text: What our grid reveals in border is in this puzzle, in message added

indicators.note: in message added puts the phrase for this puzzle inside the afterthought

blocks.note: a hem is the border of a piece of cloth
taken as written
a postscript, added to the end of a letter
here, in this very place

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about what the grid shows, concealed in a message tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the grid's design, which presumably shows two halves of a globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemispheres are the two halves of a sphere or globe, the shape the grid's pattern displays.

clue.text: Second Eros destroyed to greater extent

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the god's name is broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
the god's name taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A second statue of the love god wrecked, to a worse extent.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros is also the famous statue at Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: More so means to a greater degree, an equivalent phrase for even more.

clue.text: Fairy works to generate capital

blocks.note: a hob is a sprite or hobgoblin
works of art

explanation.surface: A fairy toils away to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of the Australian state of Tasmania.

clue.text: Bloody demise for another newspaper boss

indicators.note: a demise is an end, so only the end letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the closing letter
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A violent death awaits yet another newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloody is covered in blood, and blood is red in colour, so red describes it.

clue.text: Poet-physician’s desire to embrace daughter!

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, holding the abbreviation inside

blocks.note: Dr is the title for a doctor
a yen is a longing
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A doctor-poet longs to hug his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet and the first official Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Slip! Republican’s in East River!

indicators.note: in places the party abbreviation inside the abbreviation for the waterway

blocks.note: E for east and R for river
R is short for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician slips and falls into New York's East River.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, which is what slip means as a verb.

clue.text: An outlaw pursues student choreographer

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so those words follow the abbreviation

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
an is the indefinite article
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A fugitive chases a dance student.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Laban was a Hungarian dance theorist and choreographer who devised Labanotation.

clue.text: Seconds for glutton – minion sets Bunter’s place

indicators.note: seconds asks for the second letter of each following word

blocks.note: the second letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of comic fiction, is served second helpings by a minion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in the phrase 'in lieu of', meaning in place of.

clue.text: Tamworth residence in which soldiers lie?

indicators.note: in which says the soldiers go inside the residence

blocks.note: a Tamworth is a breed of pig, which lives in a sty
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A house in the town of Tamworth where troops lie low.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is an English town, but also a pig breed. 'Lie' looks like a verb for resting; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A story can mean a falsehood, as when a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: It’s Tees in uniform!

blocks.note: it is slang for sex appeal, SA
the setter, Tees, refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter shows off, dressed in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is this puzzle's setter, so 'Tees' gives ME. 'It' meaning sex appeal is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means unchanging and alike throughout, which is what same means.

clue.text: Opponents at table take action to get result

blocks.note: East and North are opposing players at a bridge table
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Rivals across a table go to court to get a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, North-South against East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, so it means to result.

clue.text: Glue at last on strap fixing crest put together again

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the word
fixing means holding in place, so the strap word holds the crest word
on means placed after, so the single letter follows

blocks.note: a rein is a leather strap for a horse
a cock's comb is its crest
the final letter

explanation.surface: Repairing a broken crest by gluing it onto a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: To recombine is to join elements together once more, as genes do.
